narrative.text:
This is part 2 only; even if completed and accepted, it would not certify the full guarantee or authorize strict-mode rollout. I’ll start with the required preflight and baseline checks before changing code.
The starting commit, ancestor check, ten-file diff, Bun version and digest, and Node version all match. npm reports 10.9.9; the brief gives no expected npm version.

The dispatch omits the required re-review and probe-reference paths. I’ll request them before writing probes, and continue with the independent dependency and baseline checks.
The manager’s reply supplies the missing read-only references and asks me to verify their digests and read the findings before editing. The dependency install completed with scripts disabled; the lockfile digest and all seven listed dependency versions match part 1.
Received and read the round-4 findings and probe list; the three supplied SHA-256 values match: `dba2e625530144c6eeb7e1e2ecd158c9e070795c7b548418fb74bef25e1866ac`, `7db6ffbcd04b7fe74668da86e8e19f257c9a106960486758911f07a298312781`, and `d63430a129654f7a6a5658473a3d0ab8d50833046908d7c6fd8737c950d1ddba`.
A real loopback probe reproduced an out-of-scope diagnostic leak on both engines: an accepted long credential used as a `push/event` event ID reaches `console.error` at `src/mcpl/push-handler.ts:174`. Both the random canary and the 32-digit credential leaked. The probe verifies authentication, execution of the originating rejection path, and arrival at the console sink.

That file is outside FILES. I’ll ask for scope authorization before editing; I won’t rewrite the application event or globally wrap console output to bypass the boundary.
The manager authorized exactly one additional file, `src/mcpl/push-handler.ts`, limited to proved strict diagnostic publications; legacy behavior and application objects must remain unchanged. I also confirm receipt and reading of the references, with the three supplied digests verified: `dba2e625530144c6eeb7e1e2ecd158c9e070795c7b548418fb74bef25e1866ac`, `7db6ffbcd04b7fe74668da86e8e19f257c9a106960486758911f07a298312781`, `d63430a129654f7a6a5658473a3d0ab8d50833046908d7c6fd8737c950d1ddba`.

Baseline build and typecheck pass. The existing suite reports 7,900 passed, 45 skipped, zero failures. Bun also exposes structured upgrade status through `unexpected-response`; unlike Node’s request object, its request has `abort()` but no `destroy()`. The initial status probe failed on that difference; the corrected probe passed.
The manager declined further scope expansion for now: I must complete the baseline leak matrix with no production edits, then finalize blocked-for-scope with affected sites, estimates, and a proposed split. The `push-handler.ts` authorization stands, but remains unused.
The expanded baseline probes found further SDK diagnostic leaks: channel-rejection logs and traces, feature-set-disable logs and traces, unknown-method logs, connection close events, queued tool-change notices, and server listings.

The public failed-turn probe also reproduced leaks into console output, traces, `failures.log`, a real loopback ops webhook, failure markers, and health state. It uses a tool result echoed by a local mock membrane—no external provider call. Catalogue disclosures are recorded separately as part-3 findings.
The baseline report and matrix are ready: 228 scenarios across 38 lanes, with 225 completed and three Bun socket-error fixtures explicitly marked unexercised. Each of the 2,736 lane/sink cells includes source sites, a gate, and an artifact reference.

The evidence-backed fix plan spans nine production source files plus README, exceeding the file ceiling. The worktree remains unchanged. I’m finalizing blocked-for-scope as directed, with estimates and a proposed split in the report.
The pending message repeats the instruction to read and verify the reference material; that was completed before probes or edits. The three supplied SHA-256 values matched: `dba2e625530144c6eeb7e1e2ecd158c9e070795c7b548418fb74bef25e1866ac`, `7db6ffbcd04b7fe74668da86e8e19f257c9a106960486758911f07a298312781`, and `d63430a129654f7a6a5658473a3d0ab8d50833046908d7c6fd8737c950d1ddba`. No report conclusion changes.
